excerpt: Verato sells identity resolution and master data management software that matches records about the same patient or customer across systems, mainly in healthcare.
content:
Verato makes identity resolution and master data management (MDM) software. In plain terms, it works out when records held in different systems describe the same person, so a hospital, health insurer, health information exchange or government agency can link a patient's records and keep one accurate profile. Its current product is Verato MDM Cloud, which its website pitches as a fix for fragmented identity data that hurts customer experience, growth and readiness for AI. Its homepage shows customer logos including Intermountain Health, Baylor Scott & White Health, Teladoc Health, Optum and the Pennsylvania Department of Health.

According to the company's own timeline, it was founded in 2012 as Araxid to solve identity matching problems for the government, and rebranded as Verato in 2015 to sell into the commercial sector, with Series A funding from investors including Bessemer Venture Partners and Columbia Capital. In February 2017 Verato announced a $12.5 million Series B co-led by Bessemer and Columbia Capital and said it had signed five new healthcare customers, including a national payer and three health information exchanges, as Becker's Hospital Review also reported. The timeline lists a Series C in 2018 that added healthcare investors such as Blue Heron Capital and the California Health Care Foundation.

Verato does not publish prices; it sells to organisations through demos and quotes. It is aimed at healthcare and other regulated organisations with large volumes of person records, not at small businesses. Buyers usually compare it with general MDM vendors such as Informatica and Reltio, or with the matching tools inside their electronic health record system.

We have not used Verato for this page. It brings together Verato's own website and the reporting linked under Sources, and says where each fact comes from. Nothing here is paid placement.

faq.a: It matches records about the same person across systems and maintains one trusted profile, mainly for healthcare organisations.
Its timeline says it was founded in 2012 as Araxid and rebranded as Verato in 2015.
Bessemer Venture Partners and Columbia Capital co-led its $12.5 million Series B in 2017; its timeline lists Blue Heron Capital and the California Health Care Foundation in a 2018 Series C.
